claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based alloys are primarily governed by composition-induced local lattice distortion measured by MSAD.
Differential solute effects of Cr, Mn, and Fe are primary determinants of the mechanical-property differences.
Cr increases the overall local lattice distortion.
Cr-induced lattice distortion raises the extrapolated 0 K CRSS by increasing resistance to dislocation glide.
Increased Mn and Fe promote dynamic solute pinning at elevated temperatures.
Dynamic pinning by Mn- and Fe-rich solutes produces the Portevin–Le Chatelier effect and serrated stress-strain flow.
Diffusible Mn- and Fe-rich solute atmospheres interact elastically with moving dislocations.
Below room temperature, dislocation glide is controlled by thermal activation over solute obstacles.
Below approximately 77 K, dislocation-inertial effects reduce the steepness of the CRSS increase.
At approximately 673–873 K and above, dynamic solute pinning causes serrated flow and a modest increase in CRSS.
Alloys richer in Cr will have higher extrapolated 0 K CRSS than lower-Cr alloys.
Alloys containing more Mn and Fe will exhibit a larger high-temperature PL-induced CRSS increment.
Alloys containing more Mn and Fe will exhibit more pronounced high-temperature serrated plastic flow.
Cryogenic CRSS will rise steeply relative to room-temperature CRSS and then taper near 77 K.
Extrapolated normalized 0 K CRSS, τ0/μ, will correlate with sqrt(MSAD)/b calculated by DFT.
The proposed mechanism is limited to equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based quinary, quaternary, and ternary concentrated solid solutions deformed as [1̄23]-oriented bulk single crystals in compression.

contradictions.description: The boundary says the hypothesis applies only up to temperatures where dynamic-solute/PL effects become significant, approximately above 673 K, while the mechanism and predicted outcomes explicitly address the PL regime and the intervention extends testing to 1373 K. It is therefore unclear whether the high-temperature PL regime is inside or outside the stated applicability range.
